issue.title: Add artist views by decade and overall
issue.body:
Related: #9

Pages that rank artists by their score from the Elo ratings, overall and per decade, replacing the Artist Stats and Artist Summary sheets. Needs the Elo rating engine (#7). Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. In the spreadsheet, artist rankings are grouped as 60s and 70s, 80s, 90s and 2000s, and 2010s and 2020s, plus an overall rollup. The app ranks one decade at a time instead of the paired groups.

## Scope
- An overall artist ranking list: rank, artist, score, number of rated albums.
- A per-decade artist ranking, one decade at a time with a decade picker (1950s through 2020s). Decades with few albums still render.
- The score is the engine's artist score (#7): `(sum of ratings + 1500) / (album count + 1)` over the artist's rated albums. The per-decade list uses the albums placed in that decade. Listed albums are left out.
- Open an artist to see their albums with cover, year, placement and rating.
- Scores update when a matchup is answered or a year's ranking changes.

## Acceptance
- For an artist with albums rated 1600 and 1700 the list shows a score of 1600.
- An artist with albums in several decades shows the right albums in each decade's list and all of them in the overall list.
- Answering a matchup changes the order where the two albums' artists are listed.
- Tests cover the list building for an artist with albums in several decades.

## Out of scope
- The decade top 25 album lists (separate ticket).
- Changing how artists are scored.
- Matching the spreadsheet's artist summary. The scoring differs on purpose.

issue.title: Add decade top 25 album lists
issue.body:
Per-decade lists of the 25 best albums, hand-ranked as in the spreadsheet, with covers and a rating-based suggestion for decades that have no list yet. Replaces the "Decade Top 25" columns and the By Decade sheet. Related: #8. Needs the Elo rating engine (#7). Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. In the spreadsheet 75 albums carry a decade rank, typed by hand: 25 each for the 1960s, 2000s and 2010s. The candidate flag is not used consistently, so it is not carried over.

## Scope
- A decade page listing the top 25 albums with cover, position, artist, year and rating.
- The list is hand-ranked. Any album with a ranked or honorable mention placement in that decade can go on it; the decade is the album's year page decade, not its catalog release year. There is no candidate flag.
- Add albums to the list and reorder by drag and drop, up to 25 per decade. Store each entry in the data model's decade list entry (#4).
- A decade with no list shows a suggestion: its top 25 albums by rating. The user can accept it and then reorder. A suggestion is not saved until accepted.
- Decade picker for every decade that has albums.

## Acceptance
- A decade with fewer than 25 eligible albums renders what it has.
- Reordering persists across reload, and a 26th album is refused.
- An empty decade shows the rating-based suggestion, and nothing is saved until the user accepts it.
- Tests cover list building and the suggestion for a decade.

## Out of scope
- Artist views (#8).
- Importing existing decade ranks (the import ticket).

issue.title: Write the MVP requirements spec for the album ranking app
issue.body:
Replace the "Best Albums" spreadsheet with an app where I search a catalog of albums, rank my favorites per year with cover art, and get artist and decade lists from a scoring system I can change. This ticket is the requirements spec for the MVP. It is a spec, not code. The follow-up development tickets are blocked on it.

## Today
The repo has only a README, so there is no code. The working system is the spreadsheet `Best Albums.xlsx` (kept by the user, not in the repo). What it does, read from the export:

- **Albums sheet.** One row per album, ranked or honorable mention. Columns: rank, album, artist, year, decade, honorable mention flag, decade top 25 candidate flag, decade top 25 rank, a "new" flag, points, total albums in year, year weight, weighted score. About 674 rows (294 ranked, 380 honorable mentions) across 1955 to 2024 and about 393 artists. Years run from 1 album (1983) to 41 (2019, 2021). Some years have fewer than 10 ranked albums.
- **Scoring System sheet.** Rank 1 to 10 earns 10 down to 1 point. An honorable mention earns 0.25.
- **Year weight.** Each year gets a weight from the number of albums listed that year (ranked plus honorable mentions). Fitting the sheet's values gives `weight = (N / maxN) ^ 0.25`, where `maxN` is the largest yearly count (41). It matches the sheet for N = 1, 2, 3, 20, 32 and 41. The formula itself is not in the export, so this is a fit, not a copy.
- **Weighted score.** `points x year weight` per album.
- **Ranked sheet.** A per-year grid: ranks 1 to 10 plus an unordered honorable mention list.
- **Decade top 25.** Albums flagged as candidates and given a rank 1 to 25 inside their decade. Filled for the 1960s, 2000s and 2010s.
- **Artist Stats, By Decade, Weighted Score and Artist Summary sheets.** Artist rankings, grouped as 60s and 70s, 80s, 90s and 2000s, and 2010s and 2020s, plus an overall rollup. Their formulas did not survive the export (the cells are empty), so the rollup rule is assumed to be the sum of weighted scores per artist.

The user says they have always been unhappy with the scoring system. They have not said what is wrong with it.

## Scope
Write the spec as `docs/superpowers/specs/<date>-album-ranker-mvp.md`. It should settle:

- **Users and shape.** Who uses it (one person or many), web or native, accounts or none, where data lives. Pick the simplest option that works and say why.
- **MVP features.** At least: catalog search with cover art, a per-year ranking screen (drag and drop, covers, honorable mentions), a configurable scoring system, artist views by decade and overall, decade top 25 lists, and import of the existing spreadsheet.
- **Scoring.** Keep the current rule as the default and as a regression baseline. Say which parts are configurable in the MVP (points per rank, honorable mention value, year weight curve, rollup rule). Record the open question of what the user dislikes about it, and ask them.
- **Decade top 25.** Decide whether it is a hand-ranked list (as in the sheet) or derived from weighted score.
- **Albums versus releases.** How an album in the catalog maps to one ranked entry (reissues, editions, compilations), and what happens when an album is missing from the catalog.
- **Data model outline.** Enough that the data model ticket can start.
- **Non-goals** and a **Calls I made** list for anything the user did not specify.
- **Acceptance for the whole MVP.** For example: importing the spreadsheet and applying the default scoring reproduces the spreadsheet's weighted scores.

## Scoring: open question

The user said the weights feel arbitrary but could not say more, and asked for a critique and a better option, possibly one with no scores at all. This is the Chief of Staff's read of the spreadsheet (754 rows, years 1955 to 2024; the Today section above counts about 674 albums, a gap not yet explained). The user approves the final choice, and it is a requirement of this spec.

**How it works today.** Rank 1 to 10 earns 10 to 1 points, an honorable mention earns 0.25. That is multiplied by a year weight of `(albums listed that year / max albums listed in any year) ^ 0.25`, so the busiest years (2019 and 2021, 41 albums) weigh 1.0 and one-album years weigh 0.395. Artist and decade lists sum the weighted scores.

**Problems.**

1. The year weight counts how many albums the user logged that year. That tracks how much they listened or how recent the year is, not how strong the year was.
2. The 0.25 exponent is a tuning knob with no justification.
3. A #1 album in a one-album year is worth 3.95 against 10 in a big year, though it was equally the favourite of its year.
4. Ranks are ordinal within a year, so nothing in the data can calibrate one year against another.
5. Linear points make #1 vs #2 count the same as #9 vs #10.
6. Artist totals are sums, so they reward catalogue size and volume over quality. For example The Beatles have 13 albums and 81.3 weighted points.

**Options to evaluate in this spec.**

- (a) Drop the year weight, keep rank points, and add diminishing returns to artist sums.
- (b) Add a cross-year signal, such as a tier or star rating per album, so years can be compared honestly.
- (c) Pairwise comparison with Elo or Bradley-Terry, using head-to-head matchups the UI can serve. This gives a global ranking with no hand-set weights.
- (d) Rank-based ordering with no scores at all: count of #1s, top 3s and top 10s, compared in that order.
- (e) A Bayesian or average-based artist score that separates quality from volume.

**Chief of Staff leaning.** (b) or (c) for albums, plus (e) for artists, with (a) kept as the compatibility baseline so the spreadsheet import reproduces today's numbers. The scoring engine (#7) must support swappable algorithms so this choice does not block it.

**Needed from this spec.** Compare the options, pick one for the MVP, and put the choice to the user for approval.

## Acceptance
- The spec is committed and approved by the user.
- Every item in Scope has an answer or an explicit open question.
- The follow-up tickets (scaffold, data model, catalog search, ranking UI, scoring engine, artist views, decade lists, import) still match the spec. Any ticket that no longer fits is edited or canceled.

## Out of scope
- Writing application code.
- Picking a visual design beyond what the ranking screen needs to be specified.

issue.title: Build the per-year ranking screen with drag and drop and covers
issue.body:
A page for one year where the user builds a ranked top 10, honorable mentions and a list of albums they heard but did not place, by dragging album covers, replacing the "Ranked" sheet. Needs catalog search (#5) and the data model (#4). Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. In the spreadsheet a year is a row of text: ranks 1 to 10 in order, then an unordered honorable mention list, and in many early years albums with neither (81 rows, mostly 1960 to 1981). Years can have fewer than 10 ranked albums.

## Scope
- A year page (pick any year) with three areas:
  - ten ordered rank slots with cover art,
  - an unordered honorable mention area,
  - an unordered **listed** area for albums heard that year but not placed.
- Add an album from catalog search into any area.
- Reorder by drag and drop, move between a rank slot, honorable mentions and listed, and remove. Changes save to storage.
- Show each album's current rating next to it, from the Elo engine (#7). Listed albums have no rating.
- One album, one year: adding an album that is already on another year page asks to move it.
- Create a manual album (title, artist, year) when the catalog does not have it, shown with the placeholder cover.
- Keyboard-usable reordering and touch drag, so it works without a mouse.
- Empty states for a year with no albums and for a year with fewer than 10 ranked.

## Acceptance
- Dragging an album from rank 4 to rank 1 shifts the others down by one and the order survives a page reload.
- Adding an album already on another year asks to move it, and moving it removes it from the first year.
- A year with 3 ranked albums renders with 7 empty slots and saves.
- Component or end-to-end tests cover add, reorder, move between the three areas and remove.

## Out of scope
- Computing the ratings (the Elo engine ticket).
- Artist and decade views.
- Importing the spreadsheet.

issue.title: feat: ALBUM-7 Elo rating engine and matchup screen
issue.body:
Closes #7

Ticket: [ALBUM-7](https://github.com/dbeallor/album-ranker/issues/7). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-album-7-elo-matchup.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-21-album-7-elo-matchup.md`.

Adds the Elo rating engine (`lib/elo/`, pure: update, replay with implied results, artist score, matchup picking), a loader and answer/skip/undo logic (`lib/ratings.ts`, `lib/matchups-service.ts`), and the `/matchups` screen. Ratings are replayed on each request and never stored. No schema changes.

## Proof

- **A wins between two new albums gives 1516 / 1484; a 1500 v 1500 tie changes nothing; replay is deterministic**: `lib/elo/elo.test.ts` (table) and `lib/elo/replay.test.ts` pass.

  ```
  $ npx vitest run lib/elo lib/matchups-service components/matchup-screen
   Test Files  6 passed (6)
        Tests  58 passed (58)
  ```

- **Implied results are exactly ranked over lower ranked and over honorable mention**: `impliedResults` test in `lib/elo/replay.test.ts` (fixture year with ranks 1, 2, 4, honorable mentions and a listed album).
- **Answering changes both ratings; undo restores them exactly**: `lib/matchups-service.test.ts` ("an answer moves both ratings", "undo restores the ratings exactly"), against an in-memory database; `replay.test.ts` covers the same at the engine level.
- **Never same-year, listed, or already-played pair while an unplayed one exists**: `lib/elo/pick.test.ts` and "never serves a listed or unplaced album" in `lib/matchups-service.test.ts`; the answer action refuses same-year, listed, unplaced and unknown pairs and stores nothing.
- **Artist score of albums rated 1600 and 1700 is 1600**: `lib/elo/artist-score.test.ts`.
- **Screen covered by a component test**: `components/matchup-screen.test.tsx` (pick, tie, skip, undo, counter, undo disabled at zero).

  ```
  $ npm test && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run build
  Tests  131 passed (131)   (lint and typecheck: no output; build compiled, /matchups is dynamic)
  ```

Not proven:
- The screen in a real browser: no browser test setup in the repo, and `/matchups` has no data to show until albums can be added to years (#6) or imported (#10). No screenshot.

Context size: pass skipped (not collective-wisdom)
